ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three blue straight lines slanting upward to the right, marked with pink arrows as mutually parallel; there is also a blue straight line slanting downward to the right as a transversal, intersecting these parallel lines in sequence. At the left intersection an angle 4x° is labeled, at the middle intersection an angle 56° is labeled, and on the right there is also an angle related to y, but finding x does not need to use it. Reasoning: Look only at the left and middle two intersections. Because the three straight lines slanting upward to the right are parallel, corresponding acute angles cut by the same transversal are equal, so the middle 56° can correspond to the corresponding acute angle at the left intersection. This 56° angle at the left intersection and the angle labeled 4x° are adjacent on a straight line, forming a pair of supplementary angles, therefore 4x + 56 = 180. Solving gives 4x = 124, so x = 31.
